validity.recommendation: No change to LengthKnownKm (455 km) — it exactly matches the PNGRB regulator's own Authorised Length figure for this pipeline, confirmed identically in two register editions 11 months apart. The length_ratio flag is a geometry-coverage gap, not a data error: CJHPL is a 4-branch network fanning out from a Chainsa hub, and the drawn route (185 km) evidently traces only one branch. Route creation should extend/redraw the geometry to cover all four branches rather than anything being changed here.
validity.researcher_notes: PNGRB's NGPL MIS register (authorised common-carrier gas pipeline register) lists 'Chainsa-Jhajjar-Hissar', Entity=GAIL, Authorised Length=455 km, Authorised Capacity=35 MMSCMD, Operating Length=440 km — identical in both the 30.06.2025 edition (pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20250630_NGPL.pdf) and the 31.05.2026 edition (pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf). The 455 km authorised figure is an EXACT match to the sheet's LengthKnownKm. The June-2025 edition carries an explicit footnote on this row: 'as per report submitted by GAIL, Trunk line of Chainsa-Jhajjar-Hissar (CJHPL) ... pipeline have been commissioned. However, commissioning letter for CJHPL is still awaited' — direct regulatory-source language distinguishing a 'trunk line' within the network, i.e. confirming CJHPL is not a single point-to-point line. This is corroborated independently by GAIL's own PNGRB Schedule-I capacity-declaration filing for this pipeline (gailebank.gail.co.in/Schedule1/4.html), which lists FOUR separate sections radiating from a Chainsa hub with individually declared throughput: Chainsa-Sakatpur (10.09 MMSCMD), Chainsa-Manesar (10.07), Chainsa-Hisar (2.27), Chainsa-Neemrana (7.21) — a fan-out network, not one trunk. GAIL's own corporate site (gailonline.com/Natural_Gas.html) separately lists 'Chhainsa-Jhajjar-Hissar Pipeline Network (CJPL)' at 440 km in its table of GAIL's operational gas-pipeline networks, matching the register's operating length almost exactly. url_verifier FAILs on both PNGRB register PDFs on a 'GAIL' substring test — this is the documented false-negative pattern for large PDFs (confirmed both URLs return live 200 application/pdf via curl -I; content confirmed locally via pdftotext -layout, quoted above verbatim). Given the exact match on the authorised figure plus the independent Schedule-I filing corroborating the fan-out structure, this is a route-coverage explanation, not a length correction — filed as validity rather than a fill because no cell needs to change.
